$comment: THE LAYOUT, AS DATA (RULE CFG). Every screen edge the builder, the export, the Educo app, the UAT scripts and the tests use is read from here. Change a number here and nowhere else. Rungs: 'from' is the first CSS px of the rung (the cascade runs mobile-first); keep them in ascending order. 'measure' caps a contained column on that rung; 'words' is how the Page check names its screens. heights are the HEIGHT classes (first CSS px of each, ascending: a phone on its side is under 'medium'). shell says which navigation an app screen gets (M3 / NavigationSuiteScaffold): a BAR when the width is under barBelow.width OR the height under barBelow.height, a SIDEBAR from sidebarFrom, a RAIL between; a bar holds at most barMax places (more → the last becomes 'More'); railWidth / sidebarWidth in CSS px (dp); barItemMin is the narrowest a bar place may be (em-px: it grows with the reader's text size) — a bar holds as many places as fit, up to barMax, the rest under More; barClearance is the room a scrolling screen leaves at its foot so its last line clears the bar (none beside a rail). listDetail.splitFrom is the rung where a list and its detail sit side by side (one pane with Back below it); listWidth is the list pane beside a detail (M3: 360dp). appTiles: the Educo app home's quick-action tiles sit as many across as fit at minWidth each (dp at the reader's text size), up to maxAcross. narrowestPhone is the low-cost phone a row must still fit (RULE AF). editor.dockFrom is the editor's own chrome line (panels dock from it), not a rung; labelsFrom / labelsWideFrom are where the top bar's buttons show their words (wide: under a finger, and the right-hand group); brandFrom is where the 'Box Builder' name shows; sheetWidth caps a bottom sheet. webApp.screens are the Educo web app's breakpoints (Tailwind's sm / md / lg… and xs). Tailwind reads all of these through tailwind.config.mjs, so a class says lg: or labels: and never a typed width. uat.edgeHeight is the window height the UAT uses for a rung's edge.

columns.$comment: The narrowest a column in a row is drawn, in rem: untouched (it wraps below this), sized by hand, and a page-grid block below the tablet rung.

resize.$comment: Edge drags in the editor. hugSnapPx: a size dragged back within this of the content's own size stores none (layout px). neighbourMinTracks: a grid neighbour's wrap threshold when its tracks cannot be measured. minRowPx: the least a row may be squeezed to (layout px). wrapPullPx: how far past a neighbour's floor a drag must go before it wraps (screen px).

media.$comment: A video is sized by its width and a proportion, never a stored height (RX3-2). videoRatio: a new video and the 16:9 style. portraitRatio + portraitWidthRem: the Portrait style (a phone-shaped video, narrower than a column). pagerDotFill + pagerDotRing: a page-by-page section's dots sit over a photograph the user chose, so no theme token can predict what is behind them — a white dot with a dark ring reads on any picture, and the arrows / pause are a dark disc with a light edge and white mark (pagerArrowFill, pagerArrowEdge) (rule 17: OKLCH, BDD1-26). photoWidths: the narrower copies the download makes of each photo, in CSS px, smallest first (AC-22, LE5-1). sizesWideTo: the widest screen the download measures a picture at — beside the wide rung's own edge — to tell a picture held by the content width (the same px at both: written in rem) from one that grows with the window (written in vw). videoMaxMb + videoTypes: what a background video may be when it is UPLOADED (MS-5b, BATCH LE-5) — it is published as uploaded, no transcoding, so the cap is the page's weight (RULE AF).

contentWidth.$comment: AC-9 (BATCH LE-3): the ONE content width a site's sections sit on, set in Page grid → Content width (rem). Unset = Full width (edge to edge, as before). minRem / maxRem bound the slider and any stored value; startRem is where it starts when turned on (live content widths measured on real sites: 1194–1280 px, layout-tiers SZ-5); stepRem its step.

sizes.$comment: BATCH LE-12. ratios: the Proportion gallery (SZ-4), value a CSS aspect-ratio (width / height), label its words — at least Webflow's presets (RULE BEST); Custom is offered beside them and starts at customStart. autoFitStart: the smallest card width a Grid set to As many as fit starts at (GR-2; WordPress Min. column width, Webflow auto-fit).

flow.$comment: BATCH LE-13. wrapWidth: the share of the line a picture set to Wrap words round it takes when it has no width of its own in rem (FL-3); wrapGapRem: the space between it and the words, on its open side and below; wrapBelowRem: below this width of its Stack the picture stops floating and takes the whole line (a container query, RULE AF); wrapMeasureShare: the most of the paragraphs' reading width (PARAGRAPH_MEASURE) the picture may take, so the words beside it always keep the rest (LE13-6). shapeThreshold and outlineRows: for Words follow → A cut-out's outline (FL-3b, BATCH LE-13b) the builder traces the picture into a polygon (LE13b-9: Chrome lays a url() shape out at the image's own pixel size, so it never matched the picture's fluid box) — a pixel is part of the outline when it is more opaque than shapeThreshold (0 … 1; 0.5 ignores a soft half-clear fringe), read in outlineRows bands from top to bottom. stripCard: the width a block of a Side by side set to Scroll sideways takes when it has no width of its own in rem — a part of the next one shows on a phone (FL-6). overlapSteps: how far, in rem, a section set to Overlap the section above is pulled up (PO-4), smallest first; their words are config/inspector.json flow.overlapSteps, one each.
